claim: DFW Terminal F expanded scope is 31 gates at approximately $4 billion, occupied solely by American Airlines.
source_title: DFW Airport and American Airlines Announce Acceleration and Expansion of Plans for Terminal F
supporting_excerpt: Terminal F expanded to 31 gates and approximately $4 billion, sole American Airlines occupancy.
caveat: Cost figure is a rounded planning number; final delivered cost will depend on procurement outcomes, escalation, and change orders.

claim: Original preapproved Terminal F plan was 15 gates at approximately $1.6 billion under the 2023 Use and Lease Agreement.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Prior agreement (2023): 10-year Use and Lease Agreement between DFW and American Airlines with preapproved capital investments, including a Terminal F planned as a 15-gate facility at approximately $1.6 billion.
caveat: The packet cites this as a 2023 preapproved-plan figure summarizing prior public reporting; not a live procurement cost.

claim: The DFW/American Use and Lease Agreement has been extended through 2043.
source_title: DFW Airport and American Airlines Announce Acceleration and Expansion of Plans for Terminal F
supporting_excerpt: Use and Lease Agreement extended through 2043.
denominator: term end of current U&L agreement
caveat: Public announcement summary; the executed agreement's confidential terms (MII thresholds, CPE trajectory) are not in the source.

claim: Terminal F first phase is scheduled to be operational in 2027; American Airlines will operate all 31 gates in the terminal when the program is completed in 2030.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW featuring Admirals Club lounge and Flagship services
supporting_excerpt: When completed in 2030, the airline will operate all 31 new gates in the terminal.
caveat: First-phase 2027 date is corroborated by the 2025-05-01 DFW/AA joint announcement; full-program 2030 date is from the AA 2026-07 release.

claim: DFW's Terminal F gate modules are being built offsite using a modular construction method with a reported approximately 30% cost savings versus conventional construction.
source_title: DFW Airport's Terminal F Rises With Record-Setting Modular Construction and a Scaled-Up $4B Plan to Meet Global Demand
supporting_excerpt: Modular construction saved approximately 30% versus conventional construction; the modular approach is also being applied to Terminal C and Terminal A renovations, adding 14 gates by spring 2026.
caveat: Secondary source citing DFW; the counterfactual conventional-cost baseline is not defined in detail. Treat the 30% figure as directional.

claim: American Airlines operates approximately 930 peak daily departures at DFW and serves more than 30% of its daily connecting customers and bags through DFW system-wide.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW featuring Admirals Club lounge and Flagship services
supporting_excerpt: more than 930 peak daily departures and more than 30% of the airline's daily connecting customers and checked bags.
denominator: AA peak day at DFW; AA system-wide connecting customers
caveat: 930 is a peak-day figure, not an annual average; the 30% share is system-wide connecting throughput, not DFW connecting share.

claim: American Airlines serves approximately 100,000 peak daily customers at DFW.
source_title: Doubling down on DFW: American further strengthens its Flagship hub
supporting_excerpt: 100,000 peak daily customers traveling on the more than 930 average peak DFW daily departing flights.
denominator: AA operations at DFW on a peak day
caveat: Peak-day figure — reflects the busiest days, not annual daily average. Includes both origin/destination and connecting customers.

claim: The new Admirals Club opening in DFW Terminal C is 37,000 square feet and is described by American Airlines as its largest Admirals Club to date.
source_title: American unveils next-generation premium experience at DFW featuring Admirals Club lounge and Flagship services
supporting_excerpt: the lounge will offer 37,000 square feet for customers to recharge and refuel before their flight.
caveat: Sq ft is the announced planned figure; final built area may differ. 'Largest to date' claim is AA's characterization.

claim: American Airlines has announced a Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go concept — a scaled-down offering rather than a Flagship-tier lounge — as its Terminal F lounge posture.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
page_or_section: Section 6 (American Airlines' premium repositioning at DFW)
supporting_excerpt: Terminal F lounge posture (as announced): A Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go concept — a scaled-down offering rather than a Flagship-tier lounge — is planned for Terminal F.
caveat: Whether the Provisions designation is a placeholder or a settled long-term decision is flagged as a known evidence gap in the packet.

claim: DFW carried approximately 85.7 million total passengers in 2025, down 2.4% from a 2024 record of 87.8 million; American Airlines' 2025 passenger share was 82.6% (70.8 million) with 82% of departures.
source_title: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport Statistics 2025
supporting_excerpt: 2025 total passengers 85.7M (down 2.4% from 87.8M 2024 record); American 82.6% passenger share (70.8M); American 82% of flights.
caveat: Aggregator restating DFW figures; pending confirmation against DFW official statistics release.

claim: Airport-level connecting share at DFW is reported at approximately 60%.
source_title: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport Statistics 2025
supporting_excerpt: connecting share approximately 60% at airport level.
caveat: Aggregator figure. This is airport-level connecting share and is not equivalent to American Airlines' carrier-level DFW connecting share.

claim: The DFW 70th Supplemental Bond Ordinance authorizes new debt not to exceed $3.0 billion between March 1, 2025 and February 28, 2026.
source_title: DFW Bond Ordinance filing (70th Supplemental Bond Ordinance)
supporting_excerpt: 70th Supplemental Bond Ordinance authorizes new debt not to exceed $3.0B, March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026.
airport_or_entity: Cities of Dallas and Fort Worth / DFW
denominator: new debt authorization ceiling for the stated window
caveat: Authorization ceiling, not necessarily amount issued. Actual issuances within the window determine debt service.

claim: DFW's Capital Improvement Program totals approximately $11.3 billion through FY 2030.
supporting_excerpt: CIP figure of approximately $11.3B through FY 2030.
caveat: Industry-analyst restatement of DFW disclosures; the exact underlying disclosure and its updates should be traced.

claim: KBRA has assigned an AA rating with Stable outlook to DFW's 2025A-1 (AMT), 2025A-2 (AMT), and 2025B (Non-AMT) Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds.

airport_or_entity: DFW / Cities of Dallas and Fort Worth
caveat: One rating agency; other agency ratings on the same airport system have historically differed.

claim: Terminal F's announced amenity scope includes a new centralized Skylink Station, a walking connection to Terminal D, and an expanded parking garage designed with built-in curbside circulation.
source_title: DFW Airport and American Airlines Announce Acceleration and Expansion of Plans for Terminal F
supporting_excerpt: state-of-the-art amenities; expanded shops and restaurants; a new centralized Skylink Station; walking connection to Terminal D; expanded parking garage designed with built-in curbside circulation; dedicated areas for ticketing, check-in, security screening, and baggage claim.
caveat: Announcement-level named scope; detailed sq ft and gate mix per amenity are not disclosed in the release.

supporting_excerpt: serves more than 200 million customers annually; operates more than 6,000 daily flights to more than 350 destinations.
units: flights per day; destinations; countries; annual customers
